function.name: query_upstream_lineage
function.description: Retrieves upstream (source) lineage for a given table. Finds all tables whose fields transform into any field of the target table. Results show each upstream table with its layer, schema, and hop distance.

table_name.description: The exact name of the target table. Example: "F_ACCOUNT_CONS"

max_depth.description: Maximum number of hops to traverse upstream. Default is "10". Use "1" for direct sources only.

function.name: query_downstream_lineage
function.description: Retrieves downstream (dependent) lineage for a given table. Finds all tables whose fields receive transformations from any field of the source table. Useful for impact analysis — understanding what breaks if this table changes.

table_name.description: The exact name of the source table to trace downstream. Example: "MAST_LOAN_REC"

max_depth.description: Maximum number of hops to traverse downstream. Default is "10". Use "1" for direct dependents only.

function.name: query_column_lineage
function.description: Retrieves field-level lineage showing where a specific field derives from. Traces TRANSFORMS_TO backwards to find all source fields with transformation details.

field_name.description: The exact name of the field/column to trace. Example: "DDM_SOURCE_CD"

table_name.description: The table containing this field. Example: "D_LOAN_ACCOUNT_CONS"

function.name: query_cross_layer_path
function.description: Finds the shortest lineage path between two tables across layers. Useful for tracing the full pipeline from a TPR source to a DDM target (e.g., TPR → TT → DDM).

source_table.description: The starting table (typically TPR layer). Example: "MAST_LOAN_REC"

target_table.description: The ending table (typically DDM layer). Example: "D_LOAN_ACCOUNT_CONS"

function.name: query_impact_analysis
function.description: Performs impact analysis for a given table — calculates the blast radius. Shows all downstream tables grouped by layer, with counts per layer. Useful for understanding the risk of changing or removing a table.

table_name.description: The table to analyze impact for. Example: "TT_D_PARTICIPANT"

function.name: query_tables_by_layer
function.description: Lists all tables belonging to a specific data layer with field counts. Valid layers: TPR (source system), TT (temp/staging), DDM (data mart).

function.name: run_custom_cypher
function.description: Executes a custom read-only Cypher query against the lineage graph. Use this ONLY when the other lineage functions cannot answer the question. Only MATCH and RETURN queries are allowed. CREATE, DELETE, SET, MERGE, DROP, and REMOVE operations are blocked.

cypher_query.description: A valid read-only Cypher query. Example: "MATCH (f:Field {layer:'DDM'}) RETURN DISTINCT f.table_name LIMIT 10"

function.name: search_fields
function.description: Searches for fields and tables whose names contain the given term (case-insensitive). Use this when other tools return empty results to find the correct table_name or field_name.

search_term.description: A partial or full name to search for. Can be TABLE.FIELD or SCHEMA.TABLE.FIELD dotted format. Example: "SOURCE_KEY", "F_ACCOUNTS.SOURCE_KEY"

function.name: get_edge_transformation_details
function.description: Retrieves the complete transformation chain for a specific lineage edge. Returns the full step-by-step transformation logic.

function.name: get_field_transformation_logic
function.description: Retrieves all transformation logic records where a specific field is either the source or target of a transformation. Returns expressions, lookups, filters, SQL.

field_id.description: The field identifier in SCHEMA.TABLE.FIELD or TABLE.FIELD format. Example: "CRDM_DDM.F_PARTICIPANTS.CUSTOMER_KEY"

function.name: get_mapping_transformation_details
function.description: Retrieves all edge transformation records for a specific Informatica mapping. Returns summary-level details for every field-to-field edge.

function.name: get_lookup_details_for_table
function.description: Retrieves all edges where a lookup transformation is applied to fields flowing into or out of the specified table.

table_name.description: The table name (without schema prefix). Example: "F_PARTICIPANTS"

function.name: get_edges_by_transformation_name
function.description: Searches all edges whose transformation_chain contains a step with the given transformation_name. Use when the user provides a transformation step name like "exp_Tgt_..." or "lkp_...".

transformation_name.description: The exact transformation step name. Example: "exp_Tgt_TT_D_PARTICIPANT"

function.name: get_sql_and_filter_logic
function.description: Retrieves all custom SQL queries, filter conditions, and update strategy expressions used within a specific Informatica mapping.

function.name: get_active_version_info
function.description: Returns the metadata for the currently active lineage version, including version_id, description, who approved it, and when it became active.

function.name: list_lineage_versions
function.description: Lists lineage versions tracked in the version registry, optionally filtered by lifecycle status (DRAFT, ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, REJECTED).

status.description: Optional filter: DRAFT, ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, REJECTED, or empty for all.

function.name: get_version_diff_summary
function.description: Returns the diff report for a DRAFT version showing which edges were added, removed, or changed compared to the base ACTIVE version.

draft_version_id.description: The version_id of the DRAFT to inspect. Example: "v_20260629_001"

function.name: submit_change_file
function.description: Submits a YAML patch file containing lineage changes (add/update/delete fields or edges). Creates a DRAFT version with all changes applied. Only accepts .yaml files.

file_path.description: Path to the .yaml patch file on the server filesystem.

function.name: generate_backfill_sql_for_field
function.description: Generates a backfill SQL statement for a target DDM field by tracing its full upstream lineage and assembling a CTE-based SELECT/JOIN/WHERE query.

field_id.description: The target field in SCHEMA.TABLE.FIELD or TABLE.FIELD format. Example: "CRDM_DDM.F_PARTICIPANTS.CUSTOMER_KEY" or "F_PARTICIPANTS.PARTICIPANT_KEY"
